forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: GPT-5.4 with 1M token context and 75% on OSWorld-V benchmark shows strong agent capability gains, and consensus has shifted from 'decades' to 'imminent few years'; but no lab has declared AGI and ~3.6 years remaining. Slight drift up.
forecasts.base_rate: Historical reference class: zero prior instances of a paradigm-defining AI breakthrough being publicly declared in any given ~4-year window. Superforecaster aggregates (Metaculus, Manifold) on similar AGI-by-2030 questions cluster in the 15-30% range.

factors_up.factor: GPT-5.4 autonomous multi-step workflow execution at 75% on OSWorld-V
$122B OpenAI raise plus $40B Google → Anthropic implies sustained scaling
Public statements from lab leaders increasingly confident on near-term AGI

factors_down.factor: Definitional ambiguity — '3+ researchers publicly state AGI achieved' bar is non-trivial
Benchmark saturation does not equal general intelligence; transfer to real economy lagging
Compute, energy, and data constraints become binding by 2027-2028 on current scaling laws

key_uncertainties: Whether 'AGI achieved' threshold is met by capability gains alone or requires broad economic impact recognition
Whether researcher consensus forms around any single system in the 2026-2029 window
Whether regulatory or safety pauses delay public AGI declarations
update_triggers: Any lab publicly claims AGI
METR or comparable benchmark crosses human-expert threshold across all domains
OpenAI–Microsoft AGI clause triggered (now replaced by capability gates per May 2026 reporting)

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Big Four layoffs accelerating: PwC -5,600 H1 2025, KPMG -400 US advisory and -590 UK, PwC US cutting graduate hiring by a third 'related to AI impact'. Aggregate revenues still rising (PwC +2.7%, Deloitte +4.8%), but headcount and entry-level pipelines clearly contracting. Slight drift up.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — professional services sectors disrupted by general-purpose technologies (paralegals post-LexisNexis, travel agents post-internet): ≥33% contractions typically take 10-15 years from inflection. 2030 is aggressive.

factors_up.factor: Big Four entry-level hiring cuts now explicitly attributed to AI
Shift from advisory projects to AI-tool implementation reduces billable hour volume
Continued capability gains in agentic AI (GPT-5.4 OSWorld) directly substitute for junior consultants

factors_down.factor: Aggregate Big Four revenue still growing in local currency
AI implementation work itself replaces lost advisory revenue (partnership model)
Attribution to AI vs cyclical demand softness is contested — 2+ credible analyses bar may not be met

key_uncertainties: Whether 'consultancy' is read narrowly (strategy/management) or broadly (Big Four advisory + audit + tax)
Whether 2030 baseline measures revenue or employment, and whether the comparison is real or nominal
Whether the 2+ credible analyses requirement is met
update_triggers: Big Four publishes year-over-year revenue decline
Headcount falls ≥15% from 2024 peak at any Big Four firm
FT/Economist/HBR publishes analyses attributing ≥33% decline to AI

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: PollCheck 7-poll average: Labour 19.3%, Reform 25%, Conservatives 17%. Ipsos: 74% of Britons think Starmer unlikely to win next GE. Position essentially unchanged from yesterday — kept marginally up to reflect long horizon and possibility of mean reversion.
forecasts.base_rate: Governing parties recovering from mid-term low-20s polling to largest-party finish in ~3-year window: roughly 15-25% historically, but Labour's current ~19% with a fragmented 5-way race is structurally different.

factors_up.factor: Election can be delayed until Dec 2029 — ~3.5 years for recovery
Reform vote may not survive FPTP — efficient Labour seat distribution still possible
Incumbency advantage and Reform/Conservative split on right

factors_down.factor: Labour polling well below historic recovery floor; trailing 2nd-3rd, not 2nd
Starmer favourability at deep lows; 66% want him gone before next GE
Five-party fragmentation (Lab, Con, Ref, LD, Grn all 14-25%) means seat math is volatile against Labour

key_uncertainties: Leadership change probability and identity of successor
Reform durability through to GE — does it collapse, plateau, or surge
Election timing — early call vs. running to Dec 2029
update_triggers: Labour leadership challenge
Reform sustained polling lead >30% for 3+ months
Major economic shock changing voter alignment

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Same capability signals lifting Q1 also lift Q4; with 8.6 years of horizon and continued investment ($122B OpenAI raise), probability remains high. Slight drift up.
forecasts.base_rate: Conditional on AGI being feasible (which May 2026 lab statements imply), an 8-9 year window from current frontier capability levels makes the modal forecaster estimate 60-85%.

factors_up.factor: Capability scaling continues with new compute ($122B + $40B raised by frontier labs)
Agentic capability progress (OSWorld 75%) suggests transfer beyond benchmarks
Multiple credible labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI) racing to claim AGI

factors_down.factor: Possible scaling wall in 2027-2030 forcing algorithmic rather than scale-based progress
Compute, energy, fab capacity constraints
Regulatory or safety-driven pauses on capability releases

key_uncertainties: Whether current paradigm (LLMs + RL agents) reaches AGI or whether new paradigm needed
Whether 'AGI achieved' bar is met by capability or by economic-impact recognition
Geopolitical disruption to AI supply chain (Taiwan, export controls)
update_triggers: Any lab announces AGI
Sustained slowdown in capability progress over 12+ months
TSMC disruption from Taiwan crisis

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: AEI weekly tracker continues to show PRC posturing in Bashi Channel and submarine warfare prep, but no kinetic escalation. Trump-Xi summit produced no major agreements but also no rupture. Hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Conditional on no major war, the annual probability of a Chinese kinetic move against Taiwan has been estimated at ~2-3% per year by area-studies experts. Over the remaining ~3.6 years, that aggregates to ~7-11%.

factors_up.factor: Continuous PRC military buildup and research vessel surveys around Taiwan
Xi's stated 2027 PLA modernisation deadline
US distraction in Middle East / other theatres

factors_down.factor: Massive economic costs to PRC (US think tank analysis)
Japan-South Korea-Philippines-US coordination strengthening deterrence
Taiwan defence capability improvements (HIMARS to Penghu/Dongyin)

key_uncertainties: Whether PRC perceives a closing window of opportunity
Whether Xi prioritises Taiwan unification on his current timeline
Whether US deterrence credibility remains intact
update_triggers: PRC military exercises that don't stand down within normal cycle
Taiwan declaration of independence or major political shift
Sudden US policy reversal on Taiwan commitments

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: April 2026 CPI at 2.8% (down from 3.3% March). But Bank of England April MPR now expects CPI to rise to 3.3% in Q3 and somewhat further in Q4 due to Middle East energy shock. Only 7 months to year-end. Drop probability.
forecasts.base_rate: Historical: when CPI is at 2.8% with central bank expecting it to rise, probability of crossing below 2% in next 7 months is low (single digits).

factors_up.factor: April print already dropped 0.5pp month-on-month
Core CPI now at 2.5%, suggesting underlying disinflation
Possible energy price reversal if Middle East de-escalates

factors_down.factor: BoE explicitly forecasts CPI rising to 3.3% Q3 then further in Q4
Middle East conflict keeping energy prices elevated
Services inflation typically sticky around 3-4%

key_uncertainties: Whether Middle East energy shock unwinds in H2 2026
Whether services inflation breaks below recent stickiness
Whether GBP strength offsets energy
update_triggers: Any monthly print at or below 2.2%
Material de-escalation of Middle East conflict
BoE forecast revision to bring 2026 prints below 2%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Confirmed July 31, 2026 release (5 months of box office window before Dec 31 deadline). Trailer hit 718M views in first day — biggest trailer ever. Marketing engagement implies extraordinary opening. Hold at top end.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class — modern MCU Spider-Man films: Spider-Man: No Way Home grossed $1.92B (2021). Tom Holland Spider-Man films average ~$1.1B; sequel to No Way Home with same lead and Holland's first solo since hiatus.

factors_up.factor: Record-breaking trailer engagement (718M day-one views) signals exceptional demand
5+ months of theatrical window before deadline
MCU brand recovery post-2024 with continuity returns

factors_down.factor: No Way Home included multiverse novelty that may not repeat
Theatrical attendance still below 2019 peak
Strong summer 2026 competition

key_uncertainties: Audience reception relative to multiverse predecessor
China release (and any geopolitical disruption)
Streaming window length
update_triggers: Opening weekend below $200M domestic
Negative critical and audience reception (CinemaScore <A-)
Geopolitical disruption to international rollout

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: OpenAI at $25B annualised (Feb 2026, growing). Anthropic at $30-44B (April-May 2026 reports). Combined already in $55-69B range and trajectory is steep. Reaching $70B Q4 ARR is now near-certain barring catastrophe. Hold.
forecasts.base_rate: Conditional on continued growth at observed rates (OpenAI doubling roughly every 9-12 months, Anthropic faster), combined ARR crossing $70B by Q4 2026 is the central expectation, not the tail.

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already near $55-69B by May 2026
Anthropic 80x annualised growth in Q1 2026
Enterprise deployment ($5.5B injection) accelerating revenue

factors_down.factor: Definition risk: 'most recent credible reporting of Q4 2026 ARR' may not exist by year-end
Possible enterprise contract renegotiation shocks
Black swan compute outage or geopolitical disruption

key_uncertainties: Timing of Q4 2026 ARR figures becoming publicly reported
Whether reports use 'ARR', 'annualised', or 'run-rate' consistently
Whether contracted vs realised revenue distinction matters
update_triggers: Any credible Q3 2026 report of combined ARR <$60B
Major demand collapse signal from either company
Definitional dispute over what counts

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: OBR March 2026 EFO: GDP growth 1.1% (2026), 1.6% (2027); productivity assumed to reach 1% medium-term, labour supply growth declining to 0.5% by 2030 (combined trend ~1.5%). On the borderline. Hold.
forecasts.base_rate: UK 2010-2024 real GDP growth averaged ~1.4%. 2000-2024 averaged ~1.5%. So >1.5% over a decade requires outperformance vs recent trend.

factors_up.factor: AI-driven productivity acceleration potentially adds 0.3-0.5pp
OBR's 1% productivity + 0.5% labour assumption sits right at threshold
Investment in net zero, defence and infrastructure builds capital stock

factors_down.factor: Aging demographics shrinking workforce — labour supply growth declining
Persistent UK productivity puzzle remains unresolved
Fiscal constraints limit investment scope

key_uncertainties: Magnitude and timing of AI productivity gains in services-heavy UK economy
Net migration policy through 2030s
Recession risk in early 2030s
update_triggers: OBR upgrade of trend productivity assumption above 1.2%
Productivity data showing sustained >1.5% growth pre-2030
Major recession in late 2020s pushing 2030 base lower
